title: Download assets packs instead of gen meshes
author: ElioVibe
selftext:
AI is very powerful for the code but for the 3D it's very bad optimized, expensive and the style is very averaged.

On websites like CGtrader you can find asset packs for whole games that are assorted, optimized and not expensive. Even free ones are more optimized and assorted than 3D gen assets.

3D artists are using AI to make qualitative packs bigger and cheaper than ever. Also you have hunyan for free gen meshes that is way better than Meshy. Meshy is a scam. The best generative 3D AI is free for more than a year and assets are way better especially in term of optimization and consistant style.

comments.author: ArS-13
comments.body: +1 for hunyuan it's really fun to play around with especially as you can download everything and are not totally limited as your credits refresh daily.

comments.author: Square-Yam-3772
comments.body:
there are pros and cons for both

using existing assets (especially the popular packs that everyone else is using) doesn't make your game stand out. It also takes time to find the asset pack you need. 

while gen mesh has issues, you can pretty much get whatever you need for your project so it comes in clutch in some situation. 

source: I used to be a big asset kitbasher before AI. it is not that great.

replies.author: ElioVibe
replies.body:
I know it's not that great. But AI meshes are way worse. It makes your game super bad optimized and the textures are ugly and look AI.

I highly doubt that raw AI meshes would make a game stands out .. There are thousands of new AI games everyday and AI meshes have similar patterns. Retexturing them is the bare minimum in most of case I think. Retopo is probably still mandatory to make an optimized game.


Even MCP meshes tend to all look the same. If you scroll this sub you will see that all games have the same trees.

I challenge you to send me the link of 1 game that uses raw gen meshes and that some people playing it

replies.author: Square-Yam-3772
replies.body:
if you ask Fable/Astra to generate 3d assets, those are barely serviceable 

if you go with hunyuan/meshy/tripo with topology settings, it is quite decent now i.e. characters' capes are automatically generated as separate mesh.

existing asset would normally be the best quality out of all these categories especially if you pay for a good pack

from personal experience, existing asset is almost always very generic so you are either modifying them or you have to be making a very generic game to even make use of them. Some creators went the other way and make some very unique packs and you would have the opposite problem: either you honor their visions or you try to bend the elbows to make it work

there are two mildly successful steam launches from this sub that I remember, codex mortis and some alien open world RPG game. They are not even 3d (just 2d AI gen images)

I suppose using existing assets would help if you are worried about the "ai slop" feedbacks but honestly... you trade "ai slop" for "asset flip" (anti may not be vocal about asset flipping now but that doesnt mean much)

replies.author: ElioVibe
replies.body:
If your 2 only exemples are 2D images on isometric games that means there's no games with raw Meshy assets that worked.

An AI image doesn't change anything in term of optimization compared to a non ai one. That's not the case for 3D

comments.author: CycleMother2006
comments.body:
Or learn how to clean up 3d gens.

Really depends on what your game's style is. If there are a lot of games out there with similar styles, then you'll likely find assets available for it that save you the headache of doing any cleaning up or retopping. Although you still need to be able to identify what is and isn't game ready. However if your game is more niche, the only method might be to gen it yourself or build it yourself. Agreed on Meshy being a scam though. Or at least it's very overhyped for where its quality is compared to its cheaper and better competitors.

replies.author: ElioVibe
replies.body:
Cleaning and retopologizing AI meshes is almost as long as doing them for scratch and will give a Slop visual to your game while you worked weeks on the assets do it rarely worth it.

If you are skilled enough to clean up and retopologizing AI meshes there are not much  point of not doing them from scratch. It would be a bit like generating 2D slops and spending hours fixing your generated images for a comic books when you know how to draw.

Might be some exceptions but basically AI meshes are used by random people mostly because Meshy spam ads everywhere. If Unity Asset Store or CGTrader would harass everyone with Ads Meshy would sound like a joke. I've just checked the recent asset packs and dude ..

A proof is that most of people here uses Meshy while it's one if the worse AI gen model. It's all about ads.

If you subscribe to CG trader instead of Meshy you have 1000000 assets and a lot of packs. Assets that are at the level of 2040 AI. Perfect topology and beautiful substance painter textures.

replies.author: CycleMother2006
replies.body: For Low Poly, it takes just as long if not longer, I agree. However for a highly detailed model it's not particularly close. You can do a full wrap and clean up in 10-15 minutes if you know what you're doing, for a hero character. But actually sculpting it, unless you're ungodly talented, would take half a day.

replies.author: ElioVibe
replies.body:
A retopo of a character is few hours, not few minutes.

Putting AI characters or AI retopologized Characters in a game will make the hand ultra bad optimized. Even way less optimized than an asset games.

comments.author: Gigaslavx
comments.body:
As an indie dev I'd rather go low-medium poly from scratch even procedural

Using packs makes sense if you're big and can afford to pay good

But when indie dev reuses the same assets it's gonna be a tough one, sure you can still succeed but you need to match all well but even then it might not be enough and you'll be forced to compromise and you still need a good game beside assets

Think we're safe

comments.author: VasileAndrei2929
comments.body:
Indeed, the quality and the volume do favor asset packs, especially if you're lucky and get one of those ultra good Unity Marketplace sales.

I spent a ton of money buying assets on a sale even though all my current projects are 2D games, but damn, the discounts and the number of packs they got on sale was too much for me. 

And yes, I am also a 2D/3D artist, and I can and do create some of my own assets, even sold 3D models in the past, but today I genuinely can't see myself creating an entire asset library for a new 3D game. It would take too much time to model everything, and by the end I would still have to unwrap, texture, rig, animate, import, setup, code and everything... I'm just one guy for hell sake...



Also since I'm using AI.... I can't go back to manually pushing polygons around. Sorry Blender, sorry Maya... but no. My passion was always making games, 2D and 3D art was a necessity... one that hopefully will soon be completely fulfilled by the AI 😄.



So yes, Asset Packs are a Great Value for any game developer. Totally recommend them, especially the 3D ones. Great, great value.

comments.author: Entropydemic
comments.body: Hey cool, maybe I can drop Tripo3d. I hate how they offer 20 free downloads a month but only if your models aren't rigged. Like what's the fuckin' point of streamlining the model with rigging if you can't use it? I think maybe Meshy and TripoAi are in cahoots.
